answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ladder. Each identity must answer a live challenge whose correct reply depends on a secret seed mixed with the current ledger tip; a clone sharing the same seed produces identical answers, so when two instances answer the same challenge the protocol flags the pair. Honest agents keep a private copper key off the shared channel. The attacker must provision a distinct seed and separate compute per instance, paying a fresh ember of registration work and a dedicated inlet of bandwidth each time, so cloning N identities costs N times the baseline rather than one copy.
